record.paper_title: Course 6 - Short-Range Spin Glasses: Selected Open Problems
record.original_question: For laboratory and finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses, how should theory account for aging and other anomalous dynamical behavior, especially given slow relaxation and the difficulty of determining whether a system is in or out of equilibrium?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an Edwards–Anderson short-range spin glass on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ ($d$ finite, e.g. $d=3$) with Hamiltonian
$$H(\sigma) = -\sum_{\langle x,y\rangle} J_{xy}\,\sigma_x \sigma_y, \qquad \sigma_x \in \{-1,+1\},$$
where the couplings $J_{xy}$ on nearest-neighbor bonds are i.i.d. random variables drawn from a symmetric distribution (e.g. Gaussian or $\pm 1$). Equip the spin configuration space with a stochastic single-spin-flip dynamics (e.g. heat-bath or Glauber dynamics) at inverse temperature $\beta$ in the putative spin-glass phase, started from a random initial configuration at "waiting time" $t_w = 0$.

Define the two-time autocorrelation
$$C(t_w + t,\, t_w) \;=\; \frac{1}{|\Lambda|}\sum_{x \in \Lambda} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\sigma_x(t_w+t)\,\sigma_x(t_w)\right],$$
where the expectation is over the dynamics and the disorder. Experimentally and numerically, $C(t_w + t, t_w)$ exhibits aging: for large $t_w$ it is not a function of $t$ alone but depends nontrivially on the ratio (or some scaling combination) of $t$ and $t_w$, and the system never reaches equilibrium on accessible time scales.

Problem. Develop a rigorous theoretical framework for the long-time, non-equilibrium dynamics of finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses that:
(i) derives, from the microscopic Hamiltonian above, the asymptotic form of $C(t_w+t,t_w)$ and of the associated response function $R(t_w+t,t_w)$ in the aging regime;
(ii) explains the observed violation of the fluctuation–dissipation theorem and identifies the corresponding effective temperature(s);
(iii) provides operational criteria, applicable to laboratory and simulated systems with slow relaxation, for deciding whether the system is effectively in or out of equilibrium on a given observational time window.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research articles indicate that a microscopic, analytical theory of aging and out-of-equilibrium dynamics for finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses is still lacking. Reviews from 2023–2024 explicitly state that determining the non-equilibrium dynamics of short-range spin glass models analytically from a microscopic Hamiltonian has not been achieved, and that fundamental questions about aging and the equilibration of such systems remain open, despite progress through experiments and large-scale simulations (e.g. the Janus collaboration).

status_evidence.title: Spin-glass dynamics: experiment, theory and simulation
status_evidence.snippet: Aging dynamics and slow relaxation in short-range spin glasses remain only partially understood; analytical derivation from the microscopic Hamiltonian has not been achieved.
status_evidence.claim: Aging in finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses still lacks a microscopic analytical theory.

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to the Theory of Spin Glasses
status_evidence.snippet: Open theoretical questions persist regarding extending mean-field aging results to realistic short-range systems in finite dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Extending mean-field aging theory to short-range finite-dimensional spin glasses is still an open program.
